why: Three things were being conflated: the execution grammar (the K'uhul phase cycle), the behavioural modifier (the active mode), and the output contract (how the response is shaped). Conflating them invites exactly what this architecture keeps refusing — a second lifecycle for AIML modes, or a mode quietly replacing the response format. There is one phase cycle; a mode conditions the work inside a phase; a format is selected, validated and serialized by the phases themselves.

three_layers.phase: execution grammar — the canonical C6 cycle, owned by the phase driver, never duplicated here
three_layers.mode: behavioural modifier — patterns, vectors, Micronauts and question generation inside a phase
three_layers.format: output contract — the structure of the finished response, independent of both of the above

phase_roles.Pop: initialize the response fold and capture the input
phase_roles.Wo: establish intent, context and bindings; establish the output contract if none is selected
phase_roles.Yax: expand questions, hypotheses and candidates; propose a suitable response structure
phase_roles.Xul: close the accumulator and return the response

fold.meaning: the response is a phase-folded accumulator, not a per-mode pipeline: each phase transforms the same accumulator record in order
fold.why: storing one response pipeline per mode would duplicate the fold engine and create a second execution system

formats.source: the catalog's `interaction` dimension (data/grammar/daemon-behavior-modes.v1.json), so the format axis and the mode axis cannot drift apart
formats.unset: a fold may start with no format; the phases then select one
formats.example: <teacher> and <buddy> share the phase cycle but emit a step-by-step explanation versus a casual conversational answer

selection.law: if a format is already selected, a mode operates inside it and may not replace it
selection.when_unset: Wo may establish a contract, Yax may propose a structure, Sek selects, Ch'en validates, Xul serializes
selection.proposal_not_transition: a proposal or a mode's preference is not a selection; only Sek selects, and the earlier proposal stays evidence

mode_within_format.law: a mode conditions what happens inside a phase, never the phase and never a chosen format
allowed: response style within the selected structure

invariants.RF1: there is exactly one lifecycle: every stage runs inside the canonical C6 phases, and this layer adds no second execution system
invariants.RF2: phase, mode and format stay distinct; a fold records all three and no one of them is derivable from another
invariants.RF3: a selected format is not replaceable by a mode; a mode may only refine inside it, and an attempted replacement is a typed refusal
invariants.RF4: with no format selected, Wo establishes, Yax proposes, Sek selects, Ch'en validates and Xul serializes — and a proposal never counts as a selection
invariants.RF5: each stage may run only in its own phase; a stage attempted outside its phase is refused
invariants.RF6: the response is the phase-folded accumulator: no stage may skip its predecessor, and Xul closes only a verified accumulator
invariants.RF7: serialization requires verification: Xul refuses an accumulator Ch'en has not verified
invariants.RF8: the format vocabulary is the catalog's interaction dimension; an unknown format is refused rather than approximated
invariants.RF9: a mode never changes the phase, and no stage may claim phase or commit authority
invariants.RF10: the six C6 phases and the closed 14-class XCFE node ISA are unchanged by this layer
